title: Part
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees around the X-axis, zero degrees around the Y-axis, and negative ninety degrees around the Z-axis. The translation vector should be set to (0.0, 0.0, 0.0). Next, draw the first two-dimensional sketch on the first face. Begin with the first loop by drawing the first line from (0.0, 0.0) to (0.0037, 0.0). Follow this with the second line from (0.0037, 0.0) to (0.0037, 0.0165). Then, draw the first arc from (0.0037, 0.0165) to (0.0055, 0.0183) with a midpoint at (0.0042, 0.0178). Continue with the third line from (0.0055, 0.0183) to (0.022, 0.0183), followed by the fourth line from (0.022, 0.0183) to (0.022, 0.022). Draw the fifth line from (0.022, 0.022) to (0.0018, 0.022), and then the second arc from (0.0018, 0.022) to (0.0, 0.0202) with a midpoint at (0.0005, 0.0215). Finally, draw the sixth line from (0.0, 0.0202) back to (0.0, 0.0) to close the loop. Scale the entire sketch by a factor of 0.022. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three-dimensional space by rotating it using the same Euler angles and translating it using the same translation vector. Extrude the transformed sketch 0.75 units in the direction of the normal to generate the three-dimensional model. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction of the normal. The final dimensions of the cylindrical object with a rectangular section at one end will be a length of 0.02201565557729941 units, a width of 0.02201565557729941 units, and a height of 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0037, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0037, 0.0165) \
     .threePointArc((0.0042, 0.0178), (0.0055, 0.0183)) \
     .lineTo(0.022, 0.0183) \
     .lineTo(0.022, 0.022) \
     .lineTo(0.0018, 0.022) \
     .threePointArc((0.0005, 0.0215), (0.0, 0.0202)) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r  # This will represent the final model

lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# L-angle profile extruded along X
# Cross-section in YZ plane: vertical leg up Z, horizontal leg along Y
t = 0.004  # wall thickness
L = 0.022  # leg length

# Build profile on YZ plane
profile = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .moveTo(0, 0)
    .lineTo(L, 0)
    .lineTo(L, t)
    .lineTo(t, t)
    .lineTo(t, L)
    .lineTo(0, L)
    .close()
)

r = profile.extrude(0.75)

import cadquery as cq

# Create the first rectangular part
part_1 = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0.0065, 0).lineTo(0.0205, 0).lineTo(0.0205, 0.022).lineTo(0.0065, 0.022).close() \
    .moveTo(0.0135, 0.007).lineTo(0.022, 0.007).lineTo(0.022, 0.0155).lineTo(0.0135, 0.0155).close() \
    .extrude(0.75)

# Create the second part with a cylindrical cutout
part_2 = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0.0135, 0.011).circle(0.000375).extrude(-0.125, combine=False)

# Combine both parts
r = part_1.union(part_2)
